title: India Condemns Houthi Attacks on Saudi Arabia as 'Unacceptable' Threat to Region
excerpt: New Delhi denounced Houthi strikes on Saudi civilian and economic sites that injured 73 people, warning the escalation threatens regional stability and freedom of navigation through the Bab-el-Mandeb.
body:
• India's foreign ministry condemned Houthi missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia that injured 73 civilians, calling the targeting of civilian and economic infrastructure "unacceptable."
  • MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the strikes "undermined regional security and stability and threatened freedom of navigation in the Bab-el-Mandeb."
  • The Houthis struck an airbase in Khamis Mushait and oil infrastructure in nearby cities in one of the biggest attacks on Saudi soil since the US-Israeli war on Iran began in February.
  • The escalation has raised fears of a return to full-scale conflict in Yemen, with Saudi airstrikes hitting Houthi-held areas and Pakistan warning its new defence pact with Riyadh could become operative.

India on Wednesday condemned a wave of Houthi missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia that injured 73 civilians, denouncing the targeting of civilian and economic infrastructure as "unacceptable."

Responding to media inquiries, Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said India condemned the attacks on Saudi sovereign territory. He added that such actions "undermined regional security and stability and threatened freedom of navigation in the Bab-el-Mandeb," the strait linking the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden.

Context & Background

The statement followed a condemnation from the Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs over Houthi assaults on civilian and economic sites across Abha, Jazan, Khamis Mushait, and Najran. According to Reuters, Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis struck an airbase in Khamis Mushait and oil infrastructure in nearby cities on Tuesday — one of the biggest attacks inside Saudi Arabia since the start of the US-Israeli war on Iran in February.

Saudi Arabia said the strikes caused temporary shutdowns at oil sites and injured 73 people, including women and children. In retaliation, the Houthis reported more than 30 Saudi airstrikes on Marib, Al-Jawf, Taiz, and Hodeida, according to the rebels' Almasirah television.

The fighting has escalated in recent months, raising fears of a return to broader conflict after a UN-brokered truce in 2022 largely halted years of war. In July, the Houthis declared a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia in the Red Sea, prompting the Saudi-led coalition to strike Houthi military facilities. Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces have since launched a multi-pronged offensive aimed at recapturing all Houthi-held territory.

Impact & Analysis

"India condemned the attacks on Saudi sovereign territory, especially the targeting of civilian and economic facilities."

— Randhir Jaiswal, MEA spokesperson

New Delhi's response is consistent with its long-standing position against attacks on civilian infrastructure, but the language — explicitly naming threats to freedom of navigation in the Bab-el-Mandeb — underscores what is at stake for India. Roughly a tenth of global trade passes through the Red Sea corridor, and any sustained disruption hits India's energy imports and export shipments to Europe.

Saudi Arabia, for its part, asserted its lawful right to "deploy all necessary measures" to protect its territory and called for enforcement of UN Security Council Resolutions 2216 and 2722. The kingdom also denounced ongoing Houthi attacks on commercial shipping in the Red Sea.

The conflict is also acquiring a new regional dimension. Pakistan's defence minister Khawaja Asif said an attack on any member of the newly formed Makkah Defence Alliance — signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye last month — would be treated as an attack on all, and warned the pact's collective-defence provisions could become operative. "There should be no ambiguity; there is no need for any clarity that this is a joint defence agreement," Asif told Geo TV.

Diaspora Angle

Saudi Arabia hosts one of the largest Indian expatriate communities in the world, numbering in the millions, many employed in construction, healthcare, and services across the southern provinces near the affected areas. Escalation that disrupts oil infrastructure also feeds directly into crude prices — already above $100 — that shape inflation back home.

What's Next

The near-term question is whether the 2022 truce framework can survive the current cycle of retaliation. Saudi-backed forces are pressing an offensive on the ground while Houthi strikes reach deeper into the kingdom; any miscalculation could tip the confrontation back into the full-scale war both sides have spent four years trying to avoid. New Delhi will be watching the Bab-el-Mandeb closely — and so will energy markets.
